\begin{frame}[t]{How shallow water reshapes a mobile bed}
\vspace{1.3mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Water flow} transports loose grains. Where more sediment arrives than leaves, the bed rises.
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Bed evolution} changes the surface slope that drives the water. The two balances therefore have to be solved together.
\end{columns}
\vspace{2.2mm}
\noindent\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\pdfrefxform\BedformsForm}\par
\vspace{.5mm}
\small Three flume experiments produced linear ripples, three-dimensional bedforms, and irregular ripples.
\source{\credit{rubin}}
\smallskip
\normalsize\lead{Research question} \enspace Can symmetry give exact reference flows for nearby problems?
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Two published equations for reproduction}
\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.475\textwidth}
\lead{2022 \quad Eulerian system}\par
\small One time and one spatial coordinate $(t,x)\in\R^2$. Three scalar fields $(h,u,B)$ give water depth, velocity, and bed elevation.
\begin{align*}
 h_t+(hu)_x &=0,\\
 (hu)_t+\left(hu^2+\tfrac12 gh^2\right)_x
          +gh B_x &=0,\\
 B_t+\kappa(u^m)_x &=0 .
\end{align*}
$g$ is gravity, $m$ the sediment exponent, and $\kappa$ the bedload coefficient including porosity.
\source{\credit{euler}}
\column{.475\textwidth}
\lead{2026 \quad Printed material equation}\par
\small One time and one mass coordinate $(t,s)\in\R^2$. The scalar $\phi(t,s)$ gives particle position, with $\phi_s,\phi_t>0$.
\begin{align*}
 A &= \phi_s\phi_{tt}-g\phi_{ss}/\phi_s^2,\\
 T_m &= \phi_t^{m-1}\phi_{ts}/\phi_s,\\[-1pt]
 P[\phi]&=D_tA-gm\kappa D_sT_m=0 .
\end{align*}
This is the printed equation. The physical reconstruction adds the derivative $-D_s(\phi_t A/\phi_s)$.
\source{\credit{material}}
\end{columns}
\vspace{1mm}
\divider
\smallnote{Symbols are dimensionless after scaling. Before scaling, $t$ has units of time, $x,h,B,\phi$ of length, $u$ of speed, and $s$ of length squared.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Where the exponent creates extra symmetry}
\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.47\textwidth}
\lead{Search with $m$ left symbolic}\par
\small
\begin{enumerate}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
 \item Take a general generator with unknown affine coefficients and require $\pr X(\Delta)=0$ on solutions.
 \item Split by free derivatives; treat $u^{m+k}$ as an independent monomial. This gives a linear system $\mathsf A(m)\,a=0$.
 \item The kernel can grow only where a pivot minor of $\mathsf A(m)$ vanishes or two powers coincide.
 \item Decide each candidate by solving the system again at that exact $m$.
\end{enumerate}
\column{.49\textwidth}
\lead{Result: the classification is recovered}\par\smallskip
\centering
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}\toprule
 & Candidates & Extra at $m\ge1$ & Generator\\\midrule
$E_1$ & $0,1,2,3$ & $m=3$ & $X_5$ scaling\\
$P$ & $0,\ldots,4$ & $m=1,\ 3$ & boost $t\partial_\phi$, $Y_5$\\
$E_L$ & $0,\ldots,4$ & $m=3$ & $Y_5$ (no boost)\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}\par\smallskip
\raggedright\small Generic algebras are four-dimensional. $m=3$ makes $g\kappa$ scale-invariant; at $m=1$ the boost survives only in the printed scalar.
\end{columns}
\vspace{1.5mm}
\divider
\smallnote{The same test on random $(2+1)$D and $(3+1)$D equations with a hidden coefficient finds every extra generator and reduces each case to an ODE.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{The semi-analytical reduction workflow}
\centering\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/final-delivery/contribution_workflow.pdf}\par
\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.46\textwidth}
\lead{A slice meets each orbit once locally}\par
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[x={(.80cm,.03cm)},y={(-.46cm,.30cm)},z={(0cm,.61cm)},font=\footnotesize]
  \filldraw[draw=line,fill=teal!10,opacity=.85] (0,0,0)--(4,0,0)--(4,0,2.45)--(0,0,2.45)--cycle;
  \draw[axisarrow] (0,0,0)--(4.65,0,0) node[right]{$z$};
  \draw[axisarrow] (0,0,0)--(0,3.10,0) node[above left]{$\varepsilon$};
  \draw[axisarrow] (0,0,0)--(0,0,2.85) node[above]{$F$};
  \foreach \xv/\zv in {.65/.60,1.48/1.12,2.27/1.54,3.14/1.76}{
    \draw[arrow,teal!80] (\xv,0,\zv)--(\xv,2.5,\zv);
    \fill[clay] (\xv,0,\zv) circle[radius=1.4pt];
  }
  \draw[clay,line width=.7pt] plot[smooth] coordinates
    {(.65,0,.60) (1.48,0,1.12) (2.27,0,1.54) (3.14,0,1.76)};
  \node[clay,anchor=west] at (3.25,0,1.76) {slice $\varepsilon=0$};
  \node[teal] at (2.03,2.52,2.14) {orbits};
\end{tikzpicture}\par
\raggedright\smallnote{Adapted coordinates $(\varepsilon,z,F)\in\R^3$. The invariant profile assigns one scalar $F$ to each $z$.}
\column{.51\textwidth}
\lead{Count independent variables}\par
\small If the base and point orbit ranks both equal $k$, a transverse slice leaves $d-k$ of the $d$ independent variables.
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.43\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.48\linewidth}@{}}
 $(t,x)\mapsto x$ & Ordinary differential equation\\[1.1mm]
 $(t,x,y)\mapsto(t,r)$ & PDE (rotation only, $k=1$)\\[1.1mm]
 $(t,x,y)\mapsto r$ & ODE (rotation and bed drift, $k=2$)\\
\end{tabular}
\smallskip
\small The code builds the orbit chart $(z,v)$ for any $d$ and accepts $\Delta=\mathsf M(z,v)\,\mathcal E[F](z)$ with $\det\mathsf M\ne0$. The exchange offset $b(t)$ is a conditional, vertical family, not a further quotient.
\end{columns}
{\footnotesize\color{muted}\credit{olver}\quad\credit{oliveri}\par}
\end{frame}


\begin{frame}[t]{Combining variables removes time from the profile}
\vspace{.6mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.425\textwidth}
\lead{Invariant coordinate}\par
\small For the printed scalar equation at $m=3$, the generator $X=t\partial_t-2s\partial_s$ gives
\[
 \frac{dt}{d\varepsilon}=t,\quad
 \frac{ds}{d\varepsilon}=-2s,\quad
 \frac{d\phi}{d\varepsilon}=0.
\]
Thus $\sigma=st^2$ and $\phi=F(\sigma)$ on $t>0$. With $\ell=\log t$, the generator becomes $\partial_\ell$.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{axis}[width=5.30cm,height=2.90cm,axis lines=left,axis line style={draw=muted},
 xmin=.65,xmax=1.85,ymin=0,ymax=2.75,xlabel={$t$},ylabel={$s$},
 tick label style={font=\scriptsize},label style={font=\footnotesize},
 xtick={1,1.5},ytick={0,1,2},clip=false]
 \addplot[teal,thick,domain=.72:1.80,samples=30] {.55/x^2};
 \addplot[teal,thick,domain=.72:1.80,samples=30] {.90/x^2};
 \addplot[teal,thick,domain=.72:1.80,samples=30] {1.25/x^2};
 \draw[clay,densely dashed] (axis cs:1,0)--(axis cs:1,2.35);
 \node[font=\scriptsize,clay,anchor=west] at (axis cs:1.03,2.19) {slice $t=1$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\column{.535\textwidth}
\lead{Substitution into the printed equation}\par
\small Put $p=F'(\sigma)>0$ and $\beta=3\kappa$. The chain rule gives $D_t\sigma=2\sigma/t$ and $D_s\sigma=t^2$. The two terms inside the derivatives become
\begin{align*}
 A_\sigma&=2\sigma p^2+4\sigma^2pp'-gp'/p^2,\\
 T_3 &=t^{-3}J_\sigma,\qquad
 J_\sigma=8\sigma^2p(p+\sigma p').
\end{align*}
Multiplying $P[F(\sigma)]=0$ by $t$ leaves
\[
 \boxed{2\sigma A_\sigma'-g\beta J_\sigma'=0.}
\]
Primes denote derivatives in $\sigma$. The lift $F(st^2)$ still varies in time.
\smallskip

\smallnote{The third-order equation has one independent variable. Here $(t,s)\in\R^2$ and $\varepsilon,\sigma,p,F$ are scalars.}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{A rotating tank with sediment exchange}
\vspace{.5mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.575\textwidth}
\lead{Water over an exchangeable sediment bed}\par
\small A physical three-dimensional tank is represented by depth-averaged fields on $(t,x,y)$. Use horizontal velocity $\mathbf w\in\R^2$. Depth $h$, bed thickness $B$, and mobile load $a$ are scalars. Write $C=a/h$ for concentration and $\Omega$ for the rotation rate.
\begin{align*}
 h_t+\nabla\cdot(h\mathbf w)&=0,\\
 \mathbf w_t+(\mathbf w\cdot\nabla)\mathbf w+g\nabla(h+B)
       +2\Omega\mathcal J\mathbf w-\Omega^2(x,y)&=0,\\
 B_t+\nabla\cdot\mathbf Q&=J,\\
 a_t+\nabla\cdot(a\mathbf w-D_a h\nabla C)&=-J.
\end{align*}
Here $\mathcal J$ turns velocity counterclockwise by a right angle, $D_a$ is diffusivity, and $\mathbf Q=|\mathbf w|^2(K\mathbf w-G\nabla B)$ is planar bedload. The proposed exchange rate is $J=k_da-k_eB$, with fixed deposition and release rates.
\column{.39\textwidth}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=1cm,y=1cm,font=\footnotesize]
  \filldraw[fill=clay!20,draw=clay!64] (0,0.42) ellipse (2.02 and .56);
  \fill[teal!15] (-2.02,.42) rectangle (2.02,1.43);
  \filldraw[fill=teal!11,draw=teal!63] (0,1.43) ellipse (2.02 and .56);
  \draw[clay!65,line width=.6pt] (0,.42) ++(-2.02,0) arc[start angle=180,end angle=360,x radius=2.02,y radius=.56];
  \draw[teal!58,line width=.55pt] (-2.02,.42)--(-2.02,1.43) (2.02,.42)--(2.02,1.43);
  \draw[densely dashed,muted] (-2.08,-.45)--(2.10,-.45) node[below left] {fixed datum};
  \draw[axisarrow] (0,1.45)--(0,2.83) node[above] {$\Omega\mathbf e_z$};
  \draw[arrow] (0,1.57) ++(1.20,0) arc[start angle=0,end angle=122,x radius=1.20,y radius=.27];
  \draw[|<->|,muted] (1.55,.48)--(1.55,1.40) node[midway,left]{$h$};
  \draw[|<->|,clay] (1.30,-.44)--(1.30,.37) node[midway,right]{$B$};
  \draw[clayarrow] (-.82,1.10)--(-.82,.53) node[midway,left]{$k_da$};
  \draw[arrow] (-.23,.53)--(-.23,1.10) node[midway,right]{$k_e B$};
  \node[teal,anchor=west] at (-1.89,1.15) {$a$};
\end{tikzpicture}\par\smallskip
\raggedright
\smallnote{Adding the bed and mobile-load equations conserves their total after accounting for boundary flux. Rotation leaves a $(t,r)$ system; with bed drift instead of exchange it becomes the radial ODE $(gH-V^2)H'=N$, whose saddle gives two analytic critical crossings.}
\end{columns}
\vspace{1mm}
\smallnote{Before scaling, $h,B,a$ are lengths, $C$ is a volume fraction, $k_d,k_e,\Omega$ have units of inverse time, and $D_a$ is area per time.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Selecting a solver without the exact solution}
\small Three routes share one reduced equation and exact trace: Taylor and Chebyshev series, and a grey-box gated cell whose 66 weights only shape a trace-vanishing remainder.
Admit a method if trace error $\le10^{-8}$ and residual of the original balance $\le10^{-6}$; pick the smallest residual. Exact solutions only validate.
\vspace{1.5mm}

\centering
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{5pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Case & Gated cell & Chebyshev & Taylor & Selected\\
\midrule
2022 Eulerian & $6.06\times10^{-8}$ & $4.44\times10^{-16}$ & $0$ & Taylor\\
Printed scalar $P$ & $1.30\times10^{-6}$ & $3.11\times10^{-15}$ & $3.63\times10^{-9}$ & Chebyshev\\
Material $M\to E_1$ & $7.64\times10^{-8}$ & $4.44\times10^{-16}$ & $4.44\times10^{-16}$ & Taylor\\
Rotating exchange & $1.48\times10^{-6}$ & $1.22\times10^{-15}$ & $1.11\times10^{-16}$ & Taylor\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\vspace{1.5mm}

\raggedright
\lead{The original balance decides.}
On $P$ the $t\log t$ profile limits Taylor (residual $1.9\times10^{-5}$), so Chebyshev is chosen. The gated cell has field error $1.30\times10^{-6}$ there, yet residual $1.17\times10^{-2}$.
\par\smallskip
\smallnote{Maximum field errors over four withheld traces, 401 points each. 66-parameter gated cell, one fit for all traces. \texttt{bash delivery/reproduce\_all.sh} regenerates every entry.}
\source{\credit{trefethen}}
\end{frame}



\begin{frame}[t]{Conclusion}
\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.5\textwidth}
\lead{Established}\par
\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
 \item The exponent controls the algebra: extra generators exactly at $m=3$, and at $m=1$ for the printed scalar.
 \item Bed drift $\partial_t+\alpha\partial_B$ reduces $E_1$ for every $C^2$ flux $Q(u)$; for $\alpha\ne0$ a $C^1$ profile through $U_0$ exists iff $Q'(U_0)\ne0$.
 \item Rotation and drift reduce planar SVE to one radial ODE; a saddle gives two analytic crossings.
 \item A residual rule picks the solver without the exact solution; the tank profile has a continuous error bound.
\end{itemize}
\column{.46\textwidth}
\lead{Open}\par
\small
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
 \item Classify the extra symmetries of $E_1[Q]$ for all fluxes $Q$.
 \item Non-affine and conditional symmetries (the exchange offset).
 \item Whether learning beats series at matched certified accuracy on higher-order or multi-parameter profiles.
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace Symmetry, singularities, and smooth trial maps}
\vspace{.7mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.445\textwidth}
\lead{Where singular behavior enters}\par
\small The rank of a determining matrix controls which generators are available in a fixed search class. In the separate annular bed-drift model, a critical radius occurs at $D=gH-V^2=0$ in $DH'=N$. If $D=N=0$ at a saddle, two analytic profiles cross locally.
\par\vspace{1mm}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\begin{axis}[width=5.70cm,height=2.82cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={draw=muted},
 xmin=-.24,xmax=.25,ymin=-.22,ymax=.23,xtick=\empty,ytick=\empty,
 xlabel={$r-r_*$},ylabel={$H-H_*$},label style={font=\footnotesize},
 xlabel style={at={(axis description cs:1.02,.44)},anchor=south east},
 ylabel style={at={(axis description cs:.51,1)},anchor=south}]
 \addplot[muted,dashed,samples=40,domain=-.22:.22]{(1+x)^(-2/3)-1};
 \addplot[teal,thick,domain=-.21:.21]{(-21+sqrt(141))/30*x};
 \addplot[clay,thick,domain=-.19:.19]{(-21-sqrt(141))/30*x};
 \addplot[ink,only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.5pt] coordinates {(0,0)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\smallnote{Colored lines show the two tangent directions. The dashed curve is the critical locus. The radius $r$, depth $H$, and radial speed $V$ are dimensionless scalars.}
\column{.52\textwidth}
\lead{Build smoothness into the trial map}\par
\small With $\rho=r-r_*$ and the computed branch slope $s_\pm$, take
\[
 H_\theta=H_*+s_\pm\rho+\rho^2 m_\theta(\rho).
\]
A smooth scalar remainder $m_\theta$ preserves the value and slope. Evaluate the undivided residual $DH_\theta'-N$.
\smallskip

A smooth hidden block can apply
\[
 \mathcal G(v)=v+\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\tanh(Av+b).
\]
Here $v,\alpha,b\in\R^w$ and $A\in\R^{w\times w}$. The bound $\|\alpha\|_\infty\|A\|_2<1$ makes the block invertible with a Lipschitz inverse. This is a proposed choice for the critical branch.
\source{Tao, Wang and Liu (2026)}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace How a generator acts on derivatives}
\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.455\textwidth}
\lead{Infinitesimal generator}\par
\small For base coordinates $z=(t,x)\in\R^2$ and fields $U=(u,h,B)\in\R^3$, write
\[
 X=\xi^i\partial_{z_i}+\eta^a\partial_{U^a}.
\]
Its \textbf{first prolongation} differentiates the transformed graph. On the first derivative $U_i^a$ its coefficient is
\[
 \eta_i^a=D_i\eta^a-(D_i\xi^j)U_j^a .
\]
Here $i,j$ index the two base coordinates and $a$ the three fields. A symmetry makes $\pr^{(1)}X$ tangent to the first-order equation locus.
\source{\credit{olver}}
\column{.505\textwidth}
\lead{Sediment balance under time scaling}\par
\small For the 2022 system take
\[
 X=t\partial_t-u\partial_u-2h\partial_h-2B\partial_B.
\]
Time scales by $e^\varepsilon$, velocity by $e^{-\varepsilon}$, and depth and bed by $e^{-2\varepsilon}$. Hence $B_t$ and $(u^m)_x$ scale by $e^{-3\varepsilon}$ and $e^{-m\varepsilon}$.
\smallskip

With $\Delta_B=B_t+\kappa(u^m)_x$, the tangency test gives
\[
 \left.\pr^{(1)}X\,\Delta_B\right|_{\Delta_B=0}
       =(3-m)\kappa(u^m)_x .
\]
The water balances also scale uniformly, so this is a symmetry at $m=3$.
\end{columns}
\smallskip
\smallnote{Invariance gives $tu=U(x)$ and $t^2h=H(x)$. Then $t^3[h_t+(hu)_x]=(HU)'-2H=0$.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace What the liquid-block model fits}
\small
Let $\delta=z-z_0$ and $\beta(p)=(1,\widehat p)$. Use
\[
 Y_\Theta=Y_0+\delta^k\,\beta(p)\Theta\,v_1,\qquad
 v_0=\tanh(A_0\widehat z+b_0),\quad
 v_1=v_0+\tanh(\gamma)\odot\tanh(A_1v_0).
\]
The trace lift $Y_0$ supplies initial derivatives through order $k-1$.
The factor $\delta^k$ preserves these values during training.
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.47\textwidth}
\lead{Fit the reduced equation}\par\smallskip
Use six channels, five trace values and 24 interior points per trace.
Train the feature block and readout together by SciPy least squares.
Differentiate the trial map by the chain and product rules.
\column{.49\textwidth}
\lead{Check the original equation}\par\smallskip
Compare with Chebyshev and Taylor at the same four withheld traces.
Evaluate 401 interior points per trace and report field and residual
errors after the lift.
\end{columns}
\smallskip
\smallnote{Exact solutions enter the evaluation. The equations and prescribed traces supply the fit.}
\source{Tao, Wang and Liu (2026)}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace How to compare correction work at equal accuracy}
\small
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Change the start only}\par\smallskip
Use a deterministic Lie reference or a projected learned profile in the
same coefficient space. Apply the same damped Newton correction
\[
 DG_h(c_n)\Delta c_n=-G_h(c_n),\qquad
 c_{n+1}=c_n+\alpha_n\Delta c_n .
\]
Fix the branch, grid policy, constraints, tolerances and budget.
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Measure both routes}\par\smallskip
\begin{itemize}
\item Initial defect and admissibility margins.
\item Final field error, residual, traces and flux.
\item Steps, evaluations, wall time and failures.
\item Fit, inference and fallback costs.
\end{itemize}
\end{columns}
\begin{block}{Initial milestone}
Run both routes and report the paired outcomes. Equal or worse results
for the learned start are valid outcomes. A later speed claim needs
less correction work at the same accepted accuracy.
\end{block}
\source{\credit{eshaghi}\quad\credit{li}}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace Archived fixed-feature derivative formulas}
\small
On $[z_0,z_1]$, let $Y_0$ have the given derivatives at $z_0$ and
let $\widehat z=2(z-z_0)/(z_1-z_0)-1$. Set
$d_j(z)=(z-z_0)^k v_j$, $v_j=\tanh(a_j\widehat z+b_j)$ and
$\gamma_j=2a_j/(z_1-z_0)$.
\begin{align*}
 v_j' &= \gamma_j(1-v_j^2),&
 v_j''&=-2\gamma_j v_jv_j',\\
 d_j' &= k\delta^{k-1}v_j+\delta^kv_j',&
 d_j''&=k(k-1)\delta^{k-2}v_j+2k\delta^{k-1}v_j'+\delta^kv_j''.
\end{align*}
The product gives $d_j^{(i)}(z_0)=0$ for $0\leq i<k$.
When $k=1$, the first term in $d_j''$ is omitted.
\begin{itemize}
\item Eulerian and rotating exchange cases impose one trace, so $k=1$.
\item The printed scalar case imposes $F(1)=0$ and $F'(1)=1/2$, so $k=2$.
\item Use the full differentiated trial in the ODE, and reconstruct the
physical fields with the same formulas in both routes.
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace Archived linear readout fit}
\small
For $R[Y]=\mathcal L_zY-f$, set
$Y_\Theta=Y_0+\sum_{\ell,j}\beta_\ell\Theta_{\ell j}d_j$. The matrix
columns correspond to trace component $\ell\in\{0,1\}$ and feature $j$.
\[
 M_{(p,i),(\ell,j)}=\beta_\ell(p)\mathcal L_z d_j(z_i),\qquad
 q_{(p,i)}=f(z_i,p)-\mathcal L_zY_0(z_i,p).
\]
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Case & $\mathcal L_z$ & $f(z,p)$ \\
\midrule
Eulerian & $\tfrac12\partial_z$ & $-1/4$ \\
Printed scalar & $z\partial_z^2$ & $p$ \\
Rotating exchange & $\partial_z+3$ & $9/10$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Fit $\|M\operatorname{vec}(\Theta)-q\|_2^2/120$ with SciPy least squares,
relative cutoff $10^{-12}$. All three matrices have recorded rank $24$.
Use seed $42$, slopes uniform on $[0.85,2.1]$, and shifts
$b_j=-a_j\zeta_j$ for 12 equally spaced $\zeta_j\in[-1.05,1.05]$.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace A control that needs no learned weights}
\small
\begin{block}{Rotating exchange on the exact swirl branch}
\[
 b'(t)+3b(t)=0.9,\qquad b(0)=p,\qquad
 b(t;p+\Delta p)-b(t;p)=\Delta p\,e^{-3t}.
\]
\end{block}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Classical amortization}\par\smallskip
Interpolate two exact endpoint profiles or reuse a factorization across
trace values. Both are valid deterministic controls here because the
operator is fixed and the parameter enters affinely.
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Test nonlinear correction next}\par\smallskip
Perturb the initial depth of a regular travelling-wave reference,
fix compatible boundary data, and reserve whole perturbation amplitudes
for testing. Use a separately refined solution as the reference.
\end{columns}
\smallskip
\smallnote{The three archived tests compare direct profile evaluations. The proposed nonlinear test measures correction work.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace Protocol for a nonlinear paired run}
\small
\begin{enumerate}
\item Freeze the target equation, branch and traces. Build both starts
in the same trial space. Project only the homogeneous learned
remainder and check guards after projection.
\item Run the same corrector, line search and refinement policy. Log
accepted and rejected steps, residual and Jacobian evaluations,
linear solves and wall time.
\item Evaluate on independent points. Check scaled field errors against
an independent reference, parent residuals, traces, flux and physical
margins. At critical points use the undivided equation.
\item Report acceptance over all cases and paired costs where both
succeed. Include rejects, budget stops and any deterministic fallbacks.
\end{enumerate}
\smallskip
\lead{Cost accounting}\par
Measure shared setup, offline fitting and tuning, and per-query
projection, correction and validation. Compare total cost across
specified query counts.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[t]{Backup \enspace Extending the learning route}
\small
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{More physical inputs}\par\smallskip
Encode scaled equation parameters, traces and the verified branch.
Use separate models for incompatible charts. Hold out full parameter
cases and track excursions outside the declared training region.
\column{.48\textwidth}
\lead{Nonlinear residual}\par\smallskip
Use a smooth trainable remainder with hard traces. Differentiate it
in the physical coordinate by the chain rule or automatic
differentiation. Track per-equation residuals and gradient magnitudes.
\end{columns}
\begin{block}{Keep the analytical decisions explicit}
A learned generator proposal requires prolongation verification before
use. At a radial critical point, fix the crossing branch and slope
analytically, then fit a remainder under those constraints.
\end{block}
\source{\credit{wang}\quad\credit{nagesh}}
\end{frame}
